course_name_en: Computer Science: Computer Science for Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of industrial engineering in the specialty of Mechanics.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in engineering.
Application of computer science in the field of study.
Skill in handling computers and operating systems
Understanding of the basic functioning of computers
Skill in handling computer tools for engineering
Knowledge about the fundamentals of databases
Ability to implement simple algorithms in a programming language
Knowledge of the fundamentals of structured and modular programming

syllabus_topics: Concepts and basic programming techniques applied to engineering
Functions and standard Modules. Import and use of modules.
Working with sequences: lists, tuples and strings
Lists and List of lists: Matrices
Types of parameters and return values
Concepts of value and reference in parameters
Creation and invocation of own modules
teaching_methods: Introductory activities: Activities aimed at making contact, gathering information about students, group formation, organizational tasks, as well as presenting the course.

Practices with ICT support: Activities for applying knowledge to specific situations and acquiring basic and procedural skills related to the subject of study. These are developed in special spaces with equipment provided by the School, and each student is expected to have their own laptop or one provided by the School.

Problem solving: Analysis of a real event, problem or situation in order to understand it, interpret it, solve it, generate hypotheses, contrast data, reflect, complete knowledge, diagnose it and train in alternative solution procedures.
Prior study: Reading and comprehension by the student of some topics or parts of topics to deepen their knowledge in class.
Autonomous problem solving: Resolution by the student of the different types of problems, being able to identify the effectiveness of each proposed solution method.
Lecture: Exposition by the professor of the contents on the subject of study, theoretical bases and/or guidelines for a work, exercise or project to be developed by the student.

assessment_methods.method: Practices with ICT support (solution of problems, practical exercises, and activities)

assessment_rules: Ethical behavior is expected; unethical conduct (e.g., copying, plagiarism) will result in a global grade of 0.0 for the academic year. The continuous assessment system, which students are enrolled in by default, involves three tests preferably in computer labs. To pass under continuous assessment, the weighted sum (Test 1 * 0.3 + Test 2 * 0.4 + Test 3 * 0.3) must be equal to or greater than 5. Students who do not pass the first call under continuous assessment, or those who expressly opt out, will take a single 100% exam in the second call.
